sources.title: AI observability sizing, independent composite
sources.snippet: Independent 2026 estimates put AI observability at $3.0-3.4B growing 35-40% annually. That boundary is broad: it counts model monitoring, feature drift detection and data-quality tooling for traditional machine learning, which is where the great majority of the spend still sits. Analysts caution that the headline growth rate is carried by the established ML monitoring segment and does not describe every slice within it.

sources.title: The LLM application tracing slice, sized separately
sources.snippet: Tracing and evaluation tooling for LLM applications specifically is estimated at $180-260M in 2026. Growth in this slice decelerated from above 60% in 2024 to 20-25% through 2025 and 2026. The deceleration is attributed to model providers shipping tracing and evaluation natively rather than to weakening demand for the capability itself.

sources.title: Model providers ship tracing and evals in-platform
sources.snippet: OpenAI and Anthropic both ship request tracing and evaluation dashboards inside their developer platforms at no additional cost, covering the single-provider case that describes most early-stage LLM applications. Independent tools retain an advantage where an application spans several model providers or requires retention and access controls the platforms do not offer.

sources.title: ML monitoring vendors and the LLM workload
sources.snippet: Arize and WhyLabs, both from the ML monitoring lineage, shipped LLM tracing products during 2025. Datadog added LLM observability to its APM suite in the same period, bundled for existing customers rather than sold separately.
